messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — our canary kernel bump (v2.14) triggered a perf regression on long-seq workloads. p95 token latency up ~18% on the KV-heavy traces. Seen this in nightlies and customer canary in VPC. :frowning_face:
meera: Ugh. Any idea which stage is regressing? tokenize / model_compute / kv?
sam: I pulled a flamegraph from the profiler — looks like more time in the attention kernel (matmul path) and extra memcopies during KV miss paths. Will paste the micro profile in a sec.
alex: Here's the condensed profiling snippet (from the canary job):
```
# top stacks (percent of sample time)
35%  attention_kernel_v2::matmul_exec
18%  kv_store::fetch_and_deserialize (miss paths)
12%  runtime::cpu_to_gpu_copy
8%   token_output::postprocess
```
meera: That matches: kernel V2 improves short seq but is regressing for >1024 token sequences. We should gate kernel selection by seq distribution, not force global rollout.
dilip: Agreed. We already have per-model histograms for sequence_length in the serving stats. Could we add a kernel_selector rule: if p90(seq_len) > 800, pick legacy matmul_kernel_1?
alex: Yes — propose adding a new heuristic: kernel_selector = if p90_seq > 800 then use kernel_family=legacy_longseq else prefer kernel_family=v2_shortopt. Also add a per-route opt-out label so customers can pin.
monitoring-bot: New metric emitted: redwood_runtime_kernel_selection_decision{model="redwood-7b",route="/chat.complete",decision="v2_shortopt",p90_seq="120"} 1
jia: On the metrics side, we need token-level latency breakdowns surfaced in both hosted Grafana and as an export for Private/VPC customers. Current metrics: `redwood_token_latency_seconds` with labels (model, route, stage, quantized). We should add stage labels: tokenize, kv_hit, kv_fetch, model_compute, postprocess.
sam: Example prometheus metric we rely on: `redwood_token_latency_seconds_bucket{model="redwood-7b",route="/chat.complete",stage="kv_fetch",le="0.01"}`. This gives us per-token histograms so we can compute p50/p95 for each stage.
meera: For Private/VPC customers who want their own Prometheus + Grafana, what's the plan? remote_write to customer Prometheus? scrape from an exporter in customer VPC? air-gapped tarball?
jia: Options we've discussed: 1) support Prometheus remote_write from our control-plane scrapers into the customer's Prometheus (with VPC peering and auth); 2) ship a metrics-agent that runs in the VPC and exposes /metrics for customer scraping; 3) for air-gapped, provide an export bundle (Prometheus-compatible .json + Grafana dashboard json + scripts) that customers can import periodically.
dilip: For air-gapped customers, remote_write is impossible. Export tarball needs to include metric metadata (HELP/TYPE), dashboard JSON, and promtool-friendly examples. Also include a small local exporter binary to translate our protobuf metrics into Prometheus exposition format without live network.
alex: Agree. For VPC: prefer a push model where the agent in VPC pulls local runtime metrics and forwards to the customer's Prometheus pushgateway OR writes to a locally-deployed Prometheus. We must ensure exported metric names and labels match hosted product dashboards exactly so queries are portable.
meera: @jia can you draft the Prometheus remote_write example config we can hand to customers? I want the auth and TLS bits in there.
jia: Sure — here's a starting snippet customers can use for remote_write (they run this in their Prometheus config to send to their internal storage):
```yaml
remote_write:
  - url: "https://prometheus.internal.customer.example/api/v1/write"
    remote_timeout: 30s
    tls_config:
      ca_file: "/etc/prometheus/ca.pem"
      cert_file: "/etc/prometheus/cert.pem"
      key_file: "/etc/prometheus/key.pem"
    send_exemplars: true
    queue_config:
      capacity: 250
```
meera: Looks good. For agent-based approach, we should version the exporter and document required ports. Also mention which metrics we MUST expose: `redwood_token_latency_seconds_bucket`, `redwood_tokens_per_request`, `redwood_kv_hit_rate`, `redwood_kernel_choice`, `redwood_batch_size_distribution`.
sam: Also add `redwood_inflight_requests` and `redwood_route_qps` so customers can correlate load spikes with latency.
dilip: On rollout — immediate step: disable the v2 kernel in the canary pool and revert to previous kernel for long-seq models. I'll submit the rollback flag now.
alex: Thanks. Action items:
- sam: produce a short perf regression writeup + attach flamegraphs (due EOD)
- meera: update kernel_selector heuristic PR (add p90_seq gate + route pin)
- jia: draft VPC remote_write docs + export bundle spec + Grafana dashboard export (add example dashboards for token-level stage breakouts)
- dilip: coordinate canary rollback and confirm stats after rollback
jia: For the Grafana export, I'll include:
 - dashboard: Token latency by stage (stacked heatmap)
 - panel: Per-route KPIs (p50/p95/p99 tokens and tokens_per_request)
 - templating: model & route variables so customers can re-use the dashboard
monitoring-bot: Created ticket INF-4218 "kernel v2 long-seq regression — rollback & kernel selector" assigned to sam, meera, dilip, jia
sam: I'll attach the flamegraph and a reproducible perf test (small script that runs long-seq synthetic traces).
meera: One more thought: add an alert rule for sudden change in `redwood_kernel_choice` for a given model or route (spikes in switching might indicate rollout issues).
alex: Good call. Also add a dashboard row for kernel choice time-series so ops can see rollout drift.
dilip: After rollback, let's run the private VPC full-e2e with customer's prometheus agent to validate label parity. If that passes, we can prepare the air-gapped bundle for customer A.
jia: Will do. I'll generate a sample dashboard JSON and the tarball skeleton — will post links when ready.
alex: Thanks team. Keep updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
